questions.question: A starts from a point at a speed of 30 m/s. After 3 seconds, B starts chasing A from the same point with a speed of 50 m/s. What will be the total distance (in metres) travelled by A and B before A is caught by B?
questions.solution:
Distance covered by A in 3 seconds = 30 × 3 = 90 m

Relative velocity of B w.r.t. A = (50 – 30) m/s = 20 m/s

Now, taking A to be at rest, B has to cover 90 m to catch A

⇒ Time taken by B to catch A = 90/20 = 4.5 seconds

⇒ Total distance covered by B = 4.5 × 50 = 225 m = total distance covered by A

⇒ Total distance covered by both A and B = 225 × 2 = 450 m

∴ the correct option is 2)

questions.question: If x² + y² + z² = xy + yz + zx, then what is the value of (7x + 3y – 5z)/5x?
questions.solution:
We know that,

(x + y + z)² = x² + y² + z² + 2(xy + yz + zx)

Using the given equation, we can conclude that.

⇒ (x + y + z)² = 3(xy + yz + zx)

Putting x = y = z = n [where n is any natural number]

We get,

⇒ (7x + 3y – 5z)/5x = (7 + 3 – 5) /5 = 1

∴ the correct option is 2)

questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 2 year at 20% per annum is Rs. 200. If the interest is compounded half yearly, then what is the difference (in Rs) between compound and simple interest for 1st year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

CI - SI for 2 years = P(R/100)²

⇒ 200 = P(20/100)² = P(1/5)² = P(1/25)

⇒ P = 200 × 25 = 5000 Rs.

Now,

Effective rate for SI in 1 year = 20%

Since, Interest is compounded half-yearly,

So, r = 20/2 = 10%, t = 2 cycle in 1 year

Thus,

Effective rate for CI in 2 year = 10 + 10 + (10*10)/100 = 21%

Hence, difference of interest = 21 - 20 = 1%

i.e. Difference = 1% of 5000 = 50 Rs.

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Calculation:**

⇒ CI – SI = Rs. 200

Let the principal be P

So, we have

⇒ P(1 + R/100n)ⁿt – P - (P × R × T)/100 = 200

⇒ P(1 + 20/100)² – P - (P × 20 × 2)/100 = 200

⇒ 1.44P – P – 0.4P = 200

⇒ 0.04P = 200

⇒ P = 200/0.04 = Rs. 5000

Now, the difference when compounded half yearly

⇒ [5000(1 + 20/200)² – 5000] – (5000 × 20 × 1)/100

⇒ [5000(1.1)² – 5000] – 1000

⇒ [5000(1.21) – 5000] – 1000

⇒ 6050 – 6000 = Rs. 50

∴ The correct answer is option (1).

questions.question: ΔABC is similar to ΔDEF. Length of AB is 12 cm and length of the corresponding side DE is 8 cm. What is the ratio of Perimeter of ΔABC : Perimeter of ΔDEF?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Δ ABC ∼ Δ DEF

AB = 12 cm, DE = 8 cm

**Concept used:**

Two triangles are said to be similar to each other, if

(1) their corresponding sides are proportional.

(2) their corresponding angles are equal.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66cc265efe83a9a134576b05e28fc3c3801de502fc641930f2966211e0205fd6.png] 

Here, Δ ABC and Δ DEF are similar triangles,

∴ ∠ A = ∠ D, ∠ B = ∠ E, ∠ C = ∠ F

and AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF

Then, Δ ABC ∼ Δ DEF

⇒ Perimeter of Δ ABC/Perimeter of Δ DEF = AB/DE

⇒ 12/8

⇒ 3/2

**∴ The ratio of Perimeter of ΔABC : Perimeter of ΔDEF = 3:2**

questions.question: If θ is an acute angle and tanθ – cotθ = 0, then what is the value of tan²⁶θ + cot¹⁰⁰θ?
questions.solution:
Given,

⇒ tanθ = cotθ

⇒ tanθ = 1/tanθ

⇒ tan²θ = 1

⇒ θ = 45°, -45°

Now, for θ = 45°

⇒ tan²⁶(45°) = (1)²⁶ = 1

⇒ cot¹⁰⁰(45°) = (1)¹⁰⁰ = 1

⇒ tan²⁶θ + cot¹⁰⁰θ = 1 + 1 = 2

Since the powers are even therefore we can ignore θ = -45°

∴ the correct option is 4)

questions.question: Due to increase of 33.33% in the price of apples, a customer can purchase 4 apples less for Rs. 16. What is the original price (in paise) of an apple?
questions.solution:
Let the price of one apple originally be ‘a’ paise

And,

Let the total number of apples be ‘b’

⇒ Total price of apples = ab

Rs 16 = 1600 paise

⇒ 1600 = ab (given) 

⇒ New price of one apple = a(1 + 33.33/100) = 1.3333a

After the increase in price,

⇒ Number of apples = b – 4

⇒ 1600 = 1.3333a × (b – 4)

⇒ 1600 = 1.3333a × [(1600/a) – 4]

⇒ 1600 = (4a/3) × [(1600 – 4a)/a]

⇒ 1200 = 1600 – 4a

⇒ 400 = 4a

⇒ a = 100

∴ the correct option is 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f72be33799c08d3322a2907949d25e7543e352bc7880a277f6efed7f62d7c04b.png] 

After an increase of 33.33% in the price of apples, a customer can purchase 4 apples less for Rs. 16. 

So, 33.33% of Rs. 16 is the price of 4 apples

Now price of 4 apples after increment = 16 of 33.33% 

⇒ Price of 4 apples after increment = 16 × (1/3) 

⇒ Price of one apple after increment = (16/3) × (1/4) = 4/3 

Price of one apple before increament = 4/3 × 3/4 = Rs. 1 = 100 paise 

**∴ Price of one apple before increament is 100 paise.**

And,

Let the average salary per employee be 7b

Total salary given by company = 5a × 7b = 35ab

Total number of employees after inflation = 3a

Average salary per employee after inflation = 8a

35ab – 24ab = 55000 (given)

⇒ ab = 55000/11 = 5000

Initial expenditure of company = 35ab = 35 × 5000 = 175000

questions.question: The length of diagonal BD of a parallelogram ABCD is 36 cm. P and Q are the centroids of triangle ABC and triangle ADC respectively. What is the length (in cm) of PQ?

Adding (i) and (ii)

⇒ PQ = 1/3(BD)

questions.question: If x(2x + 3) = 90 and 7y⁻¹/² + 2y⁻¹/² = y¹/² (x and y are positive numbers), then what is the value of x² + y²?
questions.solution:
Given,

⇒ x(2x + 3) = 90

⇒ 2x² + 3x – 90 = 0

⇒ 2x² – 12x + 15x – 90 = 0

⇒ 2x(x – 6) + 15(x – 6) = 0

⇒ (2x + 15)(x – 6) = 0

⇒ x = -15/2 (neglect, as it is given that x is positive)

⇒ x = 6

Also,

⇒ 7y⁻¹/² + 2y⁻¹/² = y¹/² 

⇒ 9y⁻¹/² = y¹/² 

⇒ y = 9

⇒ required value = x² + y² = 6² + 9² = 117

∴ the correct option is 3)

questions.question: What will be the net discount (in %) of two successive discounts of 15% and 35%?
questions.solution:
Let the marked price be m

Applying first discount, we get

⇒ Selling price = m × [1 – (15/100)]

⇒ Selling price = 0.85m

Applying second discount, we get

⇒ New sellingprice = 0.85m × [1 – (35/100)]

⇒ New selling price = 0.85m × 0.65

⇒ New selling price = 0.5525m

⇒ Net discount = m – new selling price = m – 0.5525m = 0.4475m

⇒ Net discount% = [0.4475m/m] × 100 = 44.75

∴ the correct option is 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__****Formula Used:**

⇒ a + b - (a × b)/100

**Calculation:**

⇒ 50 - 5.25

questions.question: a, b and c are 3 values, such that a + b = 5, b + c = 7.5 and c + a = 8.5. What will be the average of these values?
questions.solution:
Given,

⇒ a + b = 5

⇒ b + c = 7.5

⇒ c + a = 8.5

Adding all the 3 equations, we get

⇒ 2(a + b + c) = 5 + 7.5 + 8.5

⇒ a + b + c = 21/2 = 10.5

Now,

⇒ Average = (a + b + c)/3 = 10.5/3 = 3.5

questions.question: Due to increase of k% in the side, the area of a square increases by 69%. What is the value of k?
questions.solution:
Let the original length of side of a square be ‘a’

⇒ Area of original square = a²

⇒ Area of the new square = a²(1 + 69/100)

⇒ Area of the new square = 1.69a²

⇒ Length of side of new square = √(1.69a²)

⇒ Length of side of new square = 1.3a

Since, % increase in the length of side is k

⇒ k = [(1.3a – a)/a] × 100

⇒ k = 30%

∴ the correct option is 1)

questions.question: If an equilateral triangle has side 12 cm, then what is the difference (in cm) between the circumradius and in-radius?
questions.solution:
Given,

Side of an equilateral triangle (a) = 12 cm

⇒ In-radius(r) = (1/2) × a × cot(π/3)

⇒ r = (1/2) × 12 × (1/√3) = 6/√3 = 2√3 cm

Now,

⇒ Circumradius(R) = a³/4rs

Where s = semi perimeter

⇒ Semi perimeter, s = 3a/2 = 36/2 = 18 cm

⇒ R = 12³/[4 × (6/√3) × 18]

⇒ R = 1728√3/432 = 4√3 cm

Required value = R – r = 4√3 – 2√3 = 2√3 cm

∴ the correct option is 3)
